finding: We tested whether covering more source times preserves retrospective updates better than retaining only recent sources at the same count. At half copying, evenly spaced retention lowers expected squared prediction loss in only 2 of 14 half-count settings and none of the 14 quarter-count settings. Independent reconstruction, all 1,120 paired strata and both complete replays verify this supplied-law constructed-method result. Learned provenance, historical process correspondence and human intent remain unestablished.
